question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with a joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{3},\,0\le 3y\le x\le 3.
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{Y}(y).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le 3y\le x\le 3\}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154922/assets/54c803be9ecc7873f2624fc9d083997039cb651c11cc38eff6fa561ec064b7a5.png)

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{3y}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{3y}^{3}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}]}_{x=3y}^{x=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\frac{1}{3}\cdot {3}^{3}+3\cdot {y}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}(3y)^{3}-3y\cdot {y}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[9+3{y}^{2}-12{y}^{3}] \\  & =3+{y}^{2}-4{y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}3+{y}^{2}-4{y}^{3}, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
